summary: Sensho Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Otani University from circa 1962 to 1971. He was attested as a professor at Otani University in 2000.

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Toyo University, as well as under Yukitada Takeda, Ryomon, and Gokan Un'ei. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Tokyo.

Seok-hyeong Kim (b. 1904) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University from circa 1927 to 1930. He held an adjunct lectureship at Seoul National University and a professorship at Dongguk University.

Seong-Uk Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He serves as the Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Seongjoon Cheong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his Ph.D. at Dongguk University in 1999. He has served as a research fellow at the Translation Institute of Tibetan Buddhist Canon and a research professor at Uiduk University.

Seraphim Rose (1934–1982) worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Southern California, the California Institute of Integral Studies under Alan Watts, and UC Berkeley, and served in the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the United States.

Sergej Konstantinovich Bulich (1859–1921) was a linguist and Indologist. After studying at Kazan State University, Berlin, Jena, and Leipzig under scholars including Baudouin de Courtenay, he taught at Kazan and became professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Saint Petersburg State University.

Sergey Burmistrov is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who earned his D.Sci. at Saint Petersburg State University. He held teaching posts at Saint Petersburg State University and Saint Petersburg State University of Culture and Arts, and joined the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Sergey Malov (1880–1957) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and Saint Petersburg State University, directed several Kazan institutes (1917–1922), and headed the Sector of Turkic Languages at the Institute of Linguistics.

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev. He became a professor there, director of the Asiatic Museum, and permanent secretary of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences.

Sergiu Anatol Al-George (1922–1981) was a Romanian scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the University of Delhi, was a follower of Mircea Eliade, and held a post at the University of Bucharest (1971–1973).

Serinity Young (1944–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Vidya Dehejia, later holding posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History.
Sesso Oda (1901–1966) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded Zuigan Goto. His notable students included Gary Snyder and Soko Morinaga.

Seth Segall is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at Southern Illinois University Carbondale. He served as Assistant Clinical Professor at Yale School of Medicine (1981–2017) and Lecturer at Purchase College, SUNY (2012–2017).
Seton Uhlhorn is an Indologist who studied at Harvard University, where he has been a Ph.D. candidate and an instructional fellow in Hindi-Urdu.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Lee Sang-hae and held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a Ph.D. at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at Geumgang University and became an associate professor at Seoul National University.

Seungsahn Haengwon (1927–2004) was a Buddhist master who studied at Dongguk University and trained under Kobong Sunim, Keumbong, and Geum-o. He succeeded Kobong Sunim in 1957 and founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Manchester. He served as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).

Shagun Sinha is a scholar of Indology, computational studies, and linguistics. She completed her Ph.D. at Jawaharlal Nehru University under doctoral supervisor Girish Nath Jha and studied under faculty including Shashi Prabha Kumar and Ram Nath Jha.
